title: Rumpke, Circular Services and Recycle BC make MRF investments
summary: Improvements at a Florida MRF aim to capture an additional 2,000 tons of recyclables, and Ohio MRF upgrades will add 30,000 square feet of space. A brand-new MRF will open in BC in 2028.

title: E360S founder out as CEO, interim head named
summary: The Blackrock-backed company was founded by now-former CEO Danny Ardellini in 2018. He led the company to enter the U.S. market via acquisition earlier this year.

title: Trade groups ask to block SB 54 as part of existing California lawsuit
summary: The Flexible Packaging Association and the American Forest & Paper Association are among more than 20 plaintiffs requesting an injunction for the EPR program as they challenge recyclability labeling law SB 343.

title: Reworld faces pressure in Hawaiʻi, Pennsylvania but scores win in Maryland
summary: The company is drawing criticism for a fuel leak in Honolulu, and a Philadelphia council committee voted to end its disposal contract. Meanwhile, Montgomery County, Maryland, plans to extend the life of another facility.

title: Washington DC’s bottle bill won’t move this year, expected back in 2027
summary: The bill faced a short amount of time for consideration before newly elected council members would be sworn in in January, including a new mayor. American Beverage and NWRA opposed the bill.

title: Waste draws attention at COP31 amid $480M methane commitment
summary: Participating countries were unable to reach agreement on fossil fuel reductions at the annual conference. But zero waste became a priority, as did continued efforts to reduce methane from waste and other sources.

title: EPA seeks feedback on RCRA hazardous waste permitting reform
summary: The agency is soliciting comments on “all areas” of the permit process, including considerations for post-closure responsibilities, land sales and cost savings. Listening sessions are from Dec. 2-10.

title: Republic, WM pursue food-grade PP resin projects
summary: Republic plans to pursue approval for broader uses of its postconsumer PP resins produced by Blue Polymers. Meanwhile, WM inked an annual 25-million pound PP offtake deal with PureCycle, a maker of food grade resin.
